question: Can a same-bank contrast between reference-cost regression and within-group pairwise cost differences be defined without confounding labels, target scales, weighting or selection rules?
fixed_inputs: Existing V158 native B100, original450second cost labels, whole-seed split and no-stay reference fallback remain the comparison basis; no new feature search.

known_history.native_bank: V158, V159 endpoint, history80 and phase_context all use CausalReferenceResidualRegressor.
known_history.older_pairwise: V127 used AntisymmetricPairwiseActionRegressor on V123 B500 and 22 selector seeds, with range normalization and separate pressure/calibration filters; it failed and is not a matched native B100 comparison.
known_history.search_limit: Local small protocols, reports and call sites for V158/V159, 20261106 diagnostics, V127 and V150N/O; no claim that no other unpublished run exists.

work: Trace exact training labels and pair construction, including group-range normalization and reverse augmentation, in the existing two estimators.
Derive per-group total sample weight and how pair multiplication interacts with l2 and minimum leaf sample count; do not call equal tree parameters fully matched regularization without checking.
Trace pair-score aggregation, reference anchoring and no-stay fallback; preserve the 450-second cost endpoint.
Deliver one concise proposed comparison contract or explain why a clean comparison is not yet justified; do not fit during this audit.
closure: No automatic retry of phase features, threshold tuning, new labels, or closed-loop expansion.
